title: Inventory existing metrics/dashboards used in Hosted and identify what can ship in Private minimum observability pack
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Goal: compile an inventory of the metrics + Grafana dashboards currently used in Hosted/Dedicated and determine what we can safely and supportably ship as part of the Private observability minimum pack.

Why: Private installs cannot rely on Redwood’s internal telemetry stack assumptions (Mimir, centralized logs, internal label conventions, multi-tenant routing). We need a bounded-cardinality, documented set of signals that works on customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana (and air-gapped packaging), with minimal bespoke setup.

Scope:
- Review existing Hosted/Dedicated Grafana dashboards and panels used by SRE/oncall for inference runtime + control plane.
- Identify required underlying Prometheus metrics (including histograms/summaries) and current label sets.
- Note gaps for Private (missing instrumentation, high-cardinality labels, dependencies on internal data sources).
- Recommend a v1 dashboard set for Private minimum pack, plus required metric normalization/recording rules.

Out of scope:
- Building new dashboards in this ticket (tracked separately).
- Log pipeline defaults (tracked separately).

Deliverable:
- Inventory doc (dashboard -> panels -> metrics -> labels -> notes)
- Proposed “ship/not ship” decision per dashboard with rationale
- Follow-up tasks (instrumentation gaps, label reductions, recording rules) filed/linked
acceptance_criteria:
1) Inventory lists the top Hosted/Dedicated dashboards used for inference oncall and their primary panels.
2) For each dashboard/panel, required metrics are captured with current label sets and any known cardinality risks.
3) Each dashboard is tagged as: Ship as-is / Ship with modifications / Do not ship (v1), with rationale.
4) Gaps and required follow-up work are enumerated and mapped to existing/follow-up ENG tickets.
5) Inventory is reviewed by SRE (Rafael Mendes or Allison Grant) and Telemetry (Nadia Rahman or Thomas Baird).
work_notes:
Approach:
- Start from Hosted oncall playbook: “what dashboards do we open first?”
- Prioritize runtime golden signals + saturation/queueing + control plane liveness.
- For each dashboard, inspect PromQL queries to extract metric names + labels.
- Flag any dependency on:
  - internal-only labels (tenant_id, internal_cluster, shard)
  - high-cardinality labels (model, route, user, request_id)
  - internal datasources (Mimir-specific functions, Loki logs, tracing panels)

Constraints noted during inventory:
- Private Prometheus must not ingest unbounded labels (route/model/tenant). Where these are needed for usability, propose:
  - bucketing/aggregation via recording rules
  - top-K style panels (bounded)
  - allowlist configuration for “route_group” rather than raw route
- Some Hosted dashboards assume multi-region fleet view; Private needs single-cluster views by default.
- A subset of panels use log-derived metrics (Loki) for error breakdowns; in v1 Private dashboards should prefer Prometheus-native counters where possible.

Proposed v1 dashboard set (recommendations):
1) Runtime Overview (Ship with modifications)
   - Key panels: RPS, token throughput, p95/p99 latency, error rate, batch size, queue depth/backpressure, GPU utilization, GPU memory, OOM/restarts.
   - Changes needed: remove/replace route/model breakdown panels that rely on high-cardinality labels; use recording rules and/or allowlisted labels.

2) Control Plane Health (Ship with modifications)
   - Key panels: API gateway availability/latency, auth/RBAC integration errors, policy/routing service health, model registry sync errors.
   - Changes needed: replace internal “tenant” filters; ensure metrics exist for registry sync + policy evaluation latency.

3) Prometheus Scrape & Exporter Health (Ship as-is / minor edits)
   - Use standard Prometheus self-metrics + kube-state-metrics targets.

4) Kubernetes Workloads (Ship as-is)
   - Standard kube dashboards for pod restarts, CPU/mem, node pressure. Ensure we don’t fork too heavily.

5) GPU Fleet (Ship with modifications)
   - If DCGM exporter is present: show GPU utilization, memory used, PCIe RX/TX (optional), throttling (if available).
   - Changes needed: keep panels exporter-agnostic where possible; document required exporter and expected metric names.

Dashboards NOT recommended for v1 (Do not ship):
- Multi-cluster global overview dashboards (Hosted-specific)
- Tracing-centric dashboards that assume OTLP backend and sampling controls (defer to future “premium”)
- Cost attribution dashboards requiring internal billing data sources

Metrics gaps found (follow-ups):
- Runtime request metrics missing consistent label set across components (gateway vs router vs runtime).
- Need standardized histogram buckets for latency in Private; Hosted uses mixed bucket boundaries.
- Need consistent naming for queueing/backpressure signals (router queue vs runtime queue).

Output artifact: draft inventory doc and a short “decision summary” table for Product/SRE alignment.
inventory_summary:
Dashboards reviewed (Hosted/Dedicated):
- Inference Runtime: Overview, Latency, Throughput, Batching/KV cache
- Router/Policy Engine: Routing outcomes, fallback rate, queue depth
- API Gateway: Request/response codes, upstream latency, auth failures
- Control plane services: registry sync, config distribution, upgrade controller health
- GPU: utilization/memory/temperature via DCGM exporter
- Infra: Prometheus scrape health, k8s pod/node pressure

Key recurring metrics (representative):
- http_requests_total / grpc_server_handled_total (with code/status)
- request_duration_seconds_bucket (histograms)
- redwood_runtime_tokens_total, redwood_runtime_requests_total
- redwood_router_queue_depth, redwood_router_dropped_requests_total
- kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes
- DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL, DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED (when present)

Highest-risk labels observed:
- model, route, tenant_id, request_type, error_detail

Recommendation: ship dashboards with a reduced, documented label set; provide recording rules for golden signals and any panel needing grouping.
comments: 2025-05-07 (Dylan Brooks): Kicked off inventory by walking through Hosted oncall flow with Rafael. Top 3 dashboards opened during incidents: Runtime Overview, Router/Queueing, API Gateway. Will extract PromQL + metric names next and flag anything that assumes Mimir/Loki.

2025-05-10 (Thomas Baird): Please flag any query that groups by model or route directly; we should assume worst-case cardinality in Private. Prefer recording rules with allowlists or drop those breakdowns for v1.

2025-05-12 (Dylan Brooks): Initial findings: Runtime dashboard uses model+route breakdown in ~8 panels; these are likely not safe for customer Prometheus without guardrails. Suggest replacing with (a) cluster aggregate + (b) optional “route_group” label if provided by config. Logging-derived error panels rely on Loki; will replace with counters where possible.

2025-05-15 (Allison Grant): Aligning with standards: for v1, require the four golden signals at service boundary (gateway) and at runtime boundary (serving pods). Also ensure alert rules can be written without per-model labels.

2025-05-18 (Nadia Rahman): Noted inconsistency: gateway uses http_* metrics, router uses custom counters, runtime uses both. We should standardize names/labels in ENG-19143 and add recording rules in ENG-19144 so dashboards don’t need to know per-component quirks.

2025-05-21 (Dylan Brooks): Inventory doc shared in Drive; includes ship/no-ship decisions. Biggest blockers for shipping “as-is”: reliance on internal tenant labels and log-derived metrics. Filed follow-ups for metric normalization and recording rules; tagging this as ready for review.

2025-05-27 (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed. Direction looks good. For Private, keep default dashboards opinionated and simple; avoid any panel that can explode TSDB. Add a short appendix in docs: “why some breakdowns are omitted by default” so Support can set expectations.
